convergence.unimodality: Assumed by golden-section search; a finite sampled curve and interval contraction do not prove unimodality or a global optimum

selection.objective: Minimum observed unweighted L2 of all Vx/Vy surface samples over inclusive0.5–1s; peak checks do not alter selection
selection.decision_scope: Best evaluated coefficient in this golden-section search on one homogeneous central-source model; no independent proof of global optimum or solver convergence

method.amplitudes: L2/RMS and receiver peaks are velocity-sample statistics, not energy or reflection coefficients
method.peak_gates: All70 receivers: (a) t0+abs(x-350)/cR+80ms to1s, (b)0.5–1s. Edge gates can omit early returns. Maxima at different times need not be the same arrival

prefix_compatibility.meaning: Historical2s surfaces are read-only prefixes. Source samples at1s exactly match the prefix of2s forcing; same initial state, material, mesh, ABC, dt and native verified. This is provenance compatibility, not an independently rerun control.

method.beam: Average after t=tau+x/cR; directional diagnostic, not pure modal decomposition
method.timing: Historical wall times describe the complete2s runs, some with all-node fields; new wall times describe1s surface-only runs and are not a direct speed comparison
method.unimodality: Assumed by golden-section search; a finite sampled curve and interval contraction do not prove unimodality or a global optimum
method.field_output: Surface-only candidate runs; no new all-node velocity fields

source_prefix.method: Reconstruct historical 2s nodal force table, verify full SHA, then compare its first96001 samples exactly to target1s table
